subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed for all legacy ownerless rows now, or must an explicit compatibility or operator-recovery path exist before enforcing that boundary?
rationale: An ownerless row has no trustworthy plugin identity to authorize, but unconditional rejection can break existing plugin-runtime workflows after upgrade; source inspection cannot choose that security-versus-compatibility policy for maintainers.

options.title: Fail closed with recovery guidance
options.body: Reject ownerless rows, document or diagnose the operator recovery path, and require deployed proof that owned and foreign rows behave correctly.

options.title: Temporary compatibility window
options.body: Preserve narrowly bounded ownerless behavior with explicit deprecation, security rationale, tests, and a removal plan.

options.title: Pause for migration design
options.body: Hold the PR until a trustworthy ownership migration or operator-assisted assignment workflow is defined.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with recovery guidance
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless rows, document or diagnose the operator recovery path, and require deployed proof that owned and foreign rows behave correctly.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-level plugin trust and upgrade-policy choice rather than a routine implementation detail.
